notes: Unified-rule spec (scenario-meanings.md#background-subagent) for Hermes. Hermes' subagent primitive is `delegate_task`, and a top-level delegation is background BY CONSTRUCTION - _model_background_value (delegate_tool.py:3642-3655) forces background for every call the top-level agent makes and the schema's `background` field is documented DEPRECATED/IGNORED - so the tool returns a handle immediately ("{n} subagents are running in parallel in the background", delegate_tool.py:3070), the parent finishes its own reply ('dispatched'), and the consolidated batch result re-enters as a NEW turn after every child drains (async_delegation.py: completion_queue, drained by the CLI process_loop while idle). That is 3.2's defining ordering: the parent's end_turn lands BEFORE the child drain. Birth is modelled in TWO phases because hermes declares a ProcessMatcher: processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession at launch while the real sessions row (id shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>) is INSERTed ~2s later on the first user message. NO LONGER KNOWN_FAILING - re-assessed at commit 6ad7c28a. Hermes persists each delegate child as its own sessions row with parent_session_id = the parent's id (run_agent.py:606-640 _ensure_db_session, with session_db + parent_session_id injected at delegate_tool.py:1390-1391), tagged source='subagent' (platform="subagent" at delegate_tool.py:1385 -> _session_source_for_agent's platform fallback, run_agent.py:92-102). The adapter's allow-list previously read `source IN ('cli','tui')` and dropped that row; both query sites now read `source IN ('cli','tui','subagent')` (watcher.go:284, metrics.go:103), so the child surfaces carrying the ParentSessionID the watcher already resolves (watcher.go:281,378). From there the machinery is agent-agnostic and keyed only on ParentSessionID: indexParentChildren/ComputeSubagentSummary (grouped.go:90-106,266-300) count the live child, hasActiveChildren (session_detector_subagent.go:206-221) holds the parent working across its own end_turn, and reevaluateParent releases it only after the last child drains. FAITHFULNESS GATE: child_link must precede child_drain, and the parent must NOT go ready between child_link and child_drain (the held_working invariant) - if the parent went ready while a child was alive that is a daemon regression; if the parent only went ready AFTER blocking on the children inline that would be a foreground clone, which hermes cannot produce (there is no synchronous delegation - see the sibling 3.1 cell, agent=no). Two hermes-specific notes for whoever reads a failure: SubagentQuietWindow is NOT in play (isOrphanedChild os.Stats "<store>?session=<id>", the stat fails, so no child is ever fast-forwarded), and the child sharing the parent's PID is safe (assignPIDLocked exempts ParentSessionID != "" from same-PID cleanup, pid_manager.go:622-652). Observations pin neither model nor cost: the recording home's model is a human choice and irrlicht prices hermes from its own alias table, which has no entry for the locally configured gpt-5.6-luna (EstimateCostUSD returns 0 for an unpriced model, capacity.go:159-162) while Hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under subscription billing; tokens_nonzero is safe because the sessions row carries input/output aggregates.

text: The transient proc-<PID> presession minted by the process scanner appears in ready (hermes declares a ProcessMatcher, so this row exists before any store row does)
The REAL parent hermes session (a distinct id, shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>, from the sessions row INSERTed on the first user message) appears in ready
The user prompt drives the parent session ready -> working; the turn's only tool call is the single delegate_task batch

A delegate child appears as its own session - a sessions row INSERTed while the child is live, with parent_session_id = the parent's id and source='subagent', which the watcher's allow-list now admits
The detector emits parent_linked binding the background child's session_id -> the parent's session_id, so SubagentCount(parent) includes the live child

The parent's own reply ('dispatched') finishes while the detached children keep running, yet the SESSION stays working - it must NOT go ready when the parent's reply ends, because hasActiveChildren still sees a working child

The background child finishes its work and its session transitions working -> ready (its last assistant row carries finish_reason='stop', which watcher.turnIsDone marks Terminal), dropping the dashboard subagent count toward 0
Only AFTER the last background child drains does the parent session transition working -> ready
